posts.text: India's tech job market isn't "good" or "bad" right now. It's splitting in two. Naukri's September data shows: → Overall white-collar hiring: up 2% year on year → General software/IT hiring: down 4% → AI/ML hiring: up 20% In August, AI/ML hiring was up 31%, led by Hyderabad (+48%). The pattern is clear. Companies aren't hiring fewer people across the board. They're hiring for different skills. A few more signals from this week: → Global tech layoffs have crossed 1.63 lakh this year, and AI is cited in about 56% of them. → Oracle's latest round reportedly affects 1,000+ employees in India. → TCS planned only about 25,000 fresher offers for FY27, down from 44,000 last year. → GCCs (global capability centres) are still growing, with Hyderabad up 28% in August. What this means if you're a developer or fresher: Generic skills face more competition. Being "just another" full-stack or SDE profile is harder than it was. Pair your core stack (MERN, DevOps, Android, backend) with AI/LLM integration, cloud and security. Look beyond the big mass recruiters. GCCs, product companies and tier-2 cities like Coimbatore and Vadodara are showing stronger fresher growth. Watch the Q2 results: TCS (8 Oct), HCLTech (12 Oct), Infosys (23 Oct). Their headcount and fresher commentary will set the tone for the next quarter. My view: this is a skills shift, not a market collapse. The people who adapt will have the advantage. What's the one skill you're upskilling in this quarter? posts.text: My two cents on the current market: AI demand is accelerating quickly. Job ads requiring AI capability have roughly doubled over the past year, with AI skills now appearing across a significant proportion of software and data roles. AI Engineers are a clear example, with demand reportedly up around 150%. The supply of people with genuine hands-on AI experience simply isn’t keeping up. That shortage is creating a new tier of candidate. People who can genuinely build and implement AI are commanding strong packages, with some offers now including access to AI tooling and tokens. We’re also seeing experienced technical leaders getting back into the code. Even CTO-level candidates are exploring Software Engineering roles because they want to be hands-on with AI. At the same time, the broader tech market feels much quieter. The traditional domino effect of hiring has slowed down. When someone leaves, organisations are increasingly choosing to absorb the workload and “do more with less”. Job flow has slowed, salaries and contract rates have flattened, and junior and mid-level opportunities continue to decline as AI takes on tasks that previously helped develop less experienced engineers. posts.text: Every time a software project runs late, someone says the same thing. "We need to bring in more developers." It makes sense on paper. More people, more output. But a guy named Fred Brooks figured out in 1975 that it rarely works that way. Adding developers to a late project tends to make it later, not faster. New people need onboarding. The people doing the onboarding slow down. Coordination gets messier. The deadline gets worse. He called it Brooks's Law. posts.text: Skip the ATS. Connect directly. For new grads, interns, and career changers, applying online can feel like shouting into a void. Your resume might never reach a human. What if you could find the exact person hiring for your dream junior tech role and connect with them before you even apply? Here's a LinkedIn hack to do just that: 1. Go to LinkedIn's search bar. 2. Type "Recruiter" or "Hiring Manager." 3. Click "All Filters." 4. Under "Keywords," add: "junior software engineer" (or your role) AND your tech stack (e.g., "Python" or "React"). 5. Apply "Location" (your target US city/state) and "Industry." 6. Filter by "People." Now you see relevant recruiters. Next, send a personalized connection request. Don't just hit connect. Mention a specific company project you admire, a recent post of theirs, or a shared connection. Briefly state your interest in junior roles and your key skill. Example: "Hi [Name], I saw your post about [Company X]'s new project. As a new grad interested in Python/data roles, I'd love to connect." This direct approach bypasses the application black hole. You build a real connection and stand out. HireMe helps you find junior roles. This helps you get noticed for them. Who will you connect with first today? #JuniorTech #JobSearchHack #LinkedInTips #NewGrad
